newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar and stocks soar after U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar and stocks soar after U.S. jobs data.

text.p: The dollar and stock markets on both sides of the Atlantic soared on Friday after benign U.S. jobs and earnings data helped to calm worries about a possible rise in American interest rates.
The dollar climbed to its highest level against the mark and yen in years, while Wall Street surged in early trading and Europe's major bourses hit record highs.

In contrast gold prices fell to their lowest fixing price in almost four years as the bearish mood that has prevailed in the gold market for several months deepened. Bullion was fixed at $340.90 an ounce, down $1.90 from Thursday.

Wall Street took its cue from bond markets, which jumped after the U.S. Labour Department released January non-farm payrolls figures that showed an unexpected rise in the jobless rate. By 1545 GMT the Dow Industrials was up 76 points.

Although the jobs data was distorted by seasonal factors and harsh winter weather, economists seized on weakness in other parts of the report to predict the Federal Reserve would continue to hold rates steady in the coming months.
"The figures will give a lot of relief to the bond market and I think also stocks," one London analyst said.

Financial markets, attuned to hints of stronger inflation, had anxiously awaited the report for signs of whether the job market was tightening enough for employers to bid up wages, which could prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates.

The dollar opened strongly in Europe on the expectation that the world's main industrialised nations would not try to shoot it down at this weekend's meeting in Berlin of Group of Seven (G7) finance ministers and central bank governors.
It then set a fresh 32-month high at 1.6732 marks after the U.S. data and a four-year high against the yen at 124.56.
German and British government bonds leapt with U.S. treasuries following the U.S. data, which traders called the best of both worlds.

"Hourly earnings were much less than expected and the unemployment rate rose. It is fairly benign and the rally in bonds is a sigh of relief that the data were not worse," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities.
Equity markets, already bolstered by Wall Street's recovery on Thursday, also surged with bond markets.
London's FTSE 100 index climbed up into record territory through the afternoon, pushing through the key 4,300 point for the first time.

Kirit Shah, a strategist at Sanwa International in London, said he believed the FTSE 100 could test the 4,400-4,450 level over the next few months as investors anticipate steady interest rates in both the U.S. and Britain.

"As long as the market's attention is on low interest rates, equities will rally from here," Shah said. "But the market could be in for a nasty shock next quarter if the strong dollar has an impact on earnings."
French stocks hit a fresh all time high of 2,597.85 points on the CAC-40 index before slipping slightly.

Havas AGHP.PA , suspended on Thursday, opened 1.71 percent ower at 441.30 francs and then lost another nine few francs. Generale des Eaux EAUG.PA , also suspended on Thursday, opened up 2.18 percent at 750 and then surged to 775 francs for a rise of more than 5.5 percent.

The companies announced on Thursday that CGE would become the majority shareholder of Havas with 30 percent, and Havas ould become the leading shareholder in Canal Plus with 34.4 percent as part of a restructuring of their media activities.
German shares also surged to a new bourse record, buoyed by the dollar and the German debt market.
The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade over one percent higher at 3,138.01 points, up 33.87.
Floor trade ended before the U.S. data was released but the electronic market reacted strongly to the figures and rise in the dollar.
The IBIS DAX index continued its record-breaking run to stand at 3,162.15 points, up 37.37 points by 1545 GMT with no bearish signs in sight to halt its advance.
"Just look at the dollar - we've been through 1.67 marks and are now above that, U.S. non-farm payroll data was good and Wall Street is up -- a classic bull market," said one trader.
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6730 marks and 124.81 yen compared with 1.6514 marks and 123.70 yen in late European trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1545 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 43.4 points, or 1.02 percent, at 4,309.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 34.25 points, or 1.34 percent, at 2,592.68.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 33.87 points, or 1.09 percent, at 3,138.01. In later screen trading the IBIS DAX was up 37.37 point at 3,162.15
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in London Friday at $340.90 an ounce, down from Thursday's $342.80 fixing and its lowest level since April 22, 1993.
